newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese shares firm, buoyed by foreign markets.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese shares firm, buoyed by foreign markets.

text.p: 1725 GMT - Portuguese shares closed firmer in light trade, buoyed by positive sentiment on Wall Street and in Europe, dealers said. Among the most active stocks were Banco Comercial Portugues and computer company Reditus.
* PSI20 index up 0.24 percent to 4,953.03 points

* Dealers said expectations of good results for BCP drove the stock higher. It closed at 2,015 escudos, up 10, in volume of 202,071 shares. "The market believes that the negative aspects of the merger with Banco Portugues do Atlantico (BPA) are now over, and that the bank could post an ROE (return on equity) of 15 percent in 1997," said one dealer who asked not to be identified. BCP posted a ROE of 12.3 percent in 1995. The dealer gave no forecast for 1996. "BCP could hit 2,100 escudos soon as the market has woken up to this stock," said one dealer.

* Reditus shares rose on optimism over the firm's second half results, dealers said. It closed at 505 escudos, up 25, in volume of 134,789 shares. "Reditus has the support of creditor banks, and as its second half results will be better, one has to buy now while the stock is cheap," said one operator.
